title: What If Every Coral Reef on Earth Died?

scenes.text: What if every coral reef died? They cover almost nothing, yet the ocean can't cope without them.
Reefs cover about a tenth of one percent of the sea floor, yet up to a quarter of marine creatures rely on them.
About a quarter of the fish people eat spend part of their lives on reefs. Those catches would shrink.
Reefs also act as natural breakwaters against hurricanes, typhoons and tsunamis. Without them, storm waves would hit shores harder.
Reef tourism would collapse too, taking the jobs of tour operators and hotel workers with it.
Lose that thin strip, and up to a quarter of marine life loses its home. Scientists call reefs the rainforests of the sea.
